title.zh: 原子氢电荷交换Maxwellian速率系数

summary: Evaluate the saved H + H+ charge-exchange Maxwellian rate-coefficient fit from paired plasma temperature and impact energy samples in eV.

identity.relation: atomic-H charge-exchange Maxwellian rate coefficient from a bivariate logarithmic fit
identity.direction: paired plasma temperature and impact energy in eV -> rate coefficient in m^3/s
identity.definition: Sequentially clip positive temperature and nonnegative impact energy to [0.1, 2.01e4] eV. With L_T=log(T), L_E=log(E), accumulate log_rate=sum_j=0..8 sum_i=0..8 a[i,j]*L_E^j*L_T^i using the saved energy-outer, temperature-inner addition order and the saved 9x9 coefficient table. Return exp(log_rate)*1e-6 m^3/s. The output keeps the paired input shape.
identity.model: saved KN1DPy nine-by-nine bivariate logarithmic rate fit; not a velocity-mesh Maxwellian integral
identity.geometry: none; paired scalar or array material samples
identity.coordinates: temperature and impact energy in eV, with no spatial or velocity axis inferred
identity.boundary: finite real numeric inputs of identical shape; temperature strictly positive, impact energy nonnegative; source endpoint clipping in both dimensions; finite positive represented output
assumptions: The saved coefficient table and summation order are preserved on finite real inputs to support exact historical replay.
This rate fit is a separate relation from the atomic-H charge-exchange cross-section fit and from maxwellian-relative-speed-rate-average. Their numerical equivalence is not established.

The saved operator document declares positive temperature and nonnegative energy, while its implementation silently clipped violations; the maintained callable rejects them. Boolean, complex and numeric-string coercions are also excluded in line with the collision-domain real-input contract.

inputs.name: temperature_ev
inputs.description: Plasma temperature for the saved Maxwellian rate fit.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; exactly the shape of energy_ev
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; values below 0.1 or above 2.01e4 eV are clipped to the respective endpoint.

inputs.name: energy_ev
inputs.description: Impact energy paired with each temperature sample.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; exactly the shape of temperature_ev
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; zero and positive values below 0.1 or above 2.01e4 eV are clipped to the respective endpoint.

outputs.name: rate_m3_s
outputs.description: H + H+ charge-exchange Maxwellian rate coefficient evaluated by the saved fit.
outputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive on accepted inputs; no physical reference accuracy is asserted.

preconditions: The caller accepts the saved endpoint-clipping convention and supplies physically paired temperatures and impact energies.
supported: Scalar and equal-shape array evaluation of the saved atomic-H charge-exchange rate fit on or clipped to its declared domain.
excluded: Molecular-hydrogen charge exchange, CX collision frequencies, transport sources and explicit velocity-mesh averaging of a cross section.
External atomic-physics accuracy claims or physical correctness outside the saved fit's compared domain.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for non-real numeric, non-finite or unequal-shape inputs, nonpositive temperature or negative energy. Boolean, complex and numeric-string coercions are rejected.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if the derived rate is non-finite or nonpositive; no partial output is returned.

example.description: Evaluate paired finite samples and observe endpoint clipping.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.collisions import evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_charge_exchange_rate
t = np.array([0.01, 10.0, 50000.0])
e = np.array([0.0, 10.0, 50000.0])
r = evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_charge_exchange_rate(t, e)
assert r.shape == (3,) and np.all(np.isfinite(r)) and np.all(r > 0.0)
edge = evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_charge_exchange_rate(np.array([0.1, 10.0, 20100.0]), np.array([0.1, 10.0, 20100.0]))
assert np.array_equal(r, edge)
example.expected: Three positive rate coefficients with low and high values exactly equal to the clipped fit endpoints.

scope: Fixed saved reference values and an independent polyval2d evaluation verify the coefficient direction and fit on noncorner samples; the double-upper-endpoint corner is checked against the saved-order value.
Direct tests cover clipping, scalar shape, invalid domain and non-real input rejection.
Five optional SHA-gated historical replays compare finite one- and two-dimensional carriers exactly and document three rejection differences.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Maintained tests establish the discrete fit, clipping and failure contract on tested samples. SHA-gated saved replay establishes historical arithmetic agreement on the compared grids only. No external atomic-physics oracle validates the fit; whole-source D1 qualification, expert approval and distribution licensing are absent.
known_limitations: The saved package records an external atomic-physics validation_oracle_gap; the fit is not independently validated as a physical rate model.
Out-of-fit-range values silently repeat endpoint rates rather than extrapolating or failing.
The fitted rate is not derived at runtime from the separate cross-section asset or the mesh rate-average asset.
The saved bundle's strict D1 qualification is withdrawn, and public distribution licensing remains pending.
